props.description: Install the Slack chat plugin and connect Archon to Slack over Socket Mode -- works behind firewalls with no public URL needed.

text.insert: Connect Archon to Slack so you can interact with your AI coding assistant from any Slack workspace.
Slack runs as a chat plugin,

, released with Archon. The server starts the plugin as its own process and talks to it over the chat plugin protocol; the server itself contains no Slack code. You create a Slack app, set its two tokens in the server environment, and install the plugin. Docker provisions the image-provided plugin automatically when

Upgrading From the Bundled Slack Adapter
Earlier Archon versions ran Slack inside the server whenever

were set. The server no longer contains that adapter: without the
plugin, Slack stays off. When

is set and no Slack plugin is installed,
startup logs a
warning with Docker provisioning guidance and the manual install command.

In Docker, existing token configuration provisions the image-provided plugin offline on restart; no manual step is needed. The boot log names the release and why it was installed. Outside Docker, install the plugin (Step 7) and restart. Nothing else changes: the tokens, the Slack app
configuration,

stay as they are, and
existing conversations, linked identities and workspaces carry over because the plugin
keeps the platform id
